rows.speaker: some
rows.claim: Some understand the refuge sought here as protection from the effects of envy.
rows.anchor: According to some, the refuge sought in this verse is freedom from the effects of envy.

rows.speaker: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Azīz
rows.claim: The Umayyad caliph says no wrongdoer is more likely to suffer wrong than an envier.
rows.anchor: the Umayyad Caliph ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Azīz (r. 717–20) is reported to have said

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Envy is a root of evil: Satan's envy of Adam was the first sin in the celestial realm.
rows.anchor: the first sin to be committed in the celestial realm was Satan’s envy of Adam

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cain's envy of Abel was the first sin committed on earth.
rows.anchor: the first sin to be committed on earth was Cain’s envy of Abel

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who envy favors given to others oppose God's blessings.
rows.anchor: those who envy the favor bestowed upon others oppose the blessings of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah takes its name from mankind, what the Prophet is told to swear by in its first verse.
rows.anchor: this sūrah takes its name from what the Prophet is told to swear by in the first verse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Together, these two sūrahs are called al-Muʿawwidhatān, or The Two Protectors; their joint recitation is thought to protect against evil and misfortune.
rows.anchor: known as al-Muʿawwidhatān, “The Two Protectors,” since their recitation together is thought to provide protection from all manner of evil and misfortune

rows.speaker: the Prophet
rows.claim: The Prophet says God revealed verses unparalleled by any others: the two refuge sūrahs through their endings.
rows.anchor: the Prophet said, “God has sent verses down upon me of which none has seen their like

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True refuge from Satan requires recognizing God's complete sovereignty: He alone is worshipped and called upon for help.
rows.anchor: He is the only One to be worshipped and the only One upon Whom they can call for help

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting God as Lord, King, and God leads people to claim self-sufficiency, as Pharaoh does in three declarations.
rows.anchor: it is by forgetting that God is the Lord, King or Sovereign, and God of mankind that human beings arrogate self-sufficiency to themselves

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invocations direct people to seek refuge from self-sufficiency, the root of sin, by acknowledging total dependence on God.
rows.anchor: seek refuge from the illusion of self-sufficiency that is the root of all sin through acknowledging their complete dependence on God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan withdraws from the heart when a person remembers God and whispers when that person is heedless.
rows.anchor: he withdraws from the heart whenever one remembers God and whispers to it whenever one is heedless of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waswasah means quiet, repeated speech and here signifies every kind of temptation.
rows.anchor: refers to something said quietly and repeatedly. Here it is taken to indicate all manner of temptation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam and Eve's first sin was listening to Satan's whispers.
rows.anchor: The first sin of Adam and Eve was to listen to the whispers of Satan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elsewhere Satan is called the Deluder, seduces people, and causes them to forget or slip.
rows.anchor: Elsewhere Satan is described as the Deluder (31:33; 35:5); he seduces (47:25), causes people to forget

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran also says Satan makes evil seem fair, seeks to lead people astray, and incites evil.
rows.anchor: makes what is evil seem fair (6:43; 8:48; 16:63; 27:24; 29:38), desires to lead astray (4:60), and incites to evil (12:100)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many verses describe Satan as a manifest enemy.
rows.anchor: described in many verses as a manifest enemy (e.g., 2:168, 208; 6:142; 7:22; 12:5; 17:53)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here the whisperer is Satan, unlike other passages where the soul whispers, prompts evil, or seduces; the reference is to the passionate soul that commands evil.
rows.anchor: the reference here is not to the soul as such, but to the passionate soul, or the soul that commands to evil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary cites a famous ḥadīth saying that Satan flows in the blood of Adam's son.
rows.anchor: a famous ḥadīth says, “Truly Satan flows in the blood of the son of Adam”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One perspective is that Satan suggests and tempts, while the passionate soul follows its caprices instead of God's commands.
rows.anchor: it is Satan who suggests, tempts, prompts, and whispers, and the passionate soul then follows the caprices that arise rather than the commands of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative perspective is that only the soul commanding evil has this propensity.
rows.anchor: From another perspective, only the soul that commands to evil has this propensity

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning blindly from remembrance brings a satanic companion; related passages discuss the soul that commands evil.
rows.anchor: whosoever turns blindly away from the remembrance of the Compassionate, We assign to him a satan who is then a companion unto him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes the verse as referring to whatever whispers into the souls of jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: what whispers into the souls of jinn and mankind

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading refers to jinn whispering to people and people heeding their own whispering souls instead of God's guidance, failing to take God as Lord, King, and God.
rows.anchor: the jinn who whisper into the souls of people and to people who heed the advice of their own whispering soul rather than the Guidance of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may refer to both jinn and people who whisper into souls; both human and jinn satans are mentioned elsewhere.
rows.anchor: a reference to both the jinn and people who whisper into souls

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may refer to whispers entering the breasts of jinn and humans: although nās usually means humans, a ḥadīth speaks of a people among the jinn, as rijāl can also mean jinn individuals.
rows.anchor: word rijāl, which usually designates human men, is also used in reference to individuals

rows.speaker: Sh
rows.claim: A further reading understands verses 5–6 as seeking refuge from the one who whispers into human breasts and from jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: seeking refuge from the jinn and from mankind (Sh)
